prompt:
Edit the supplied ContextLedger Permission System diagram (the sole reference image is the EDIT TARGET). Create an updated polished English presentation slide, landscape 16:9, high resolution, with the same visual identity: soft off-white/mint background, emerald arrows and thin line icons, navy/black headings, muted slate explanatory text, white rounded cards, restrained mint glows. Keep "ContextLedger" top left, the large title "Permission System", and the small page badge "02" top right. Maintain the recognisable left-to-right architecture, but re-layout the cards to fit the updated rules cleanly with large readable type; do not simply cram text into the old cards.

Subtitle, exact: "Enforce source ACLs, project membership, clearance and local restrictions"

Composition: five main vertical groups across the slide, linked clearly by emerald arrows. The second group is wider than the first. The retrieval group contains two stacked parallel cards. Candidate IDs and authorised excerpts are arrow labels, not invented databases. Include a compact bottom revocation strip. Generous spacing and clear separation, no crossing arrows or text overlaps.

GROUP 1 heading: "Current identity"
Four white mini-cards with appropriate outline icons:
"Source bindings" / "Mapped source principal"
"Project memberships" / "e.g. SwiftUI Telemetry"
"Department & clearance" / "Engineering · Confidential (2)"
"Local restrictions" / "Source, project, department, document"
Small bottom note: "Admin role does not grant document access"

GROUP 2 heading: "Build access filters"
Subheading: "ALL applicable conditions must pass"
Four distinct rule cards, with the following exact text:
1. "Source ACL · Slack"
   "Source identity must be in the resource ACL"
   "Slack: channel ACL or DM participants"
2. "Project membership"
   "Tagged → project membership required"
   "Untagged → no project restriction"
3. "Clearance & department"
   "classification ≤ user clearance"
   "Match department when restricted"
4. "Local denies"
   "Block source, project, department or document"
Footer inside this group: "Original source ACLs still apply"
These are backend deterministic rules, not model interpretation. Avoid any depiction of LLM assigning access, automatic project detection, or 'everyone can read' for untagged documents.

GROUP 3:
A small "User question" card above two parallel retrieval cards.
Top retrieval card: "Qdrant" / "Vector search" / "Apply access filters"
Bottom retrieval card: "SQL FTS" / "Keyword search" / "Apply the same access rules"
The user question feeds both retrieval routes. The filter column also feeds both retrieval routes. Their outputs merge on one arrow labelled "Candidate IDs" going to SQLite. Neither retrieval route sends raw unfiltered content to the model.

GROUP 4 heading: "SQLite"
Subtitle: "Read canonical source text"
Three mini-cards:
"Current access" / "Recheck source ACLs and all restrictions"
"Version & hash" / "Verify canonical version and content"
"Parent access" / "Check parent document for comments"
One outbound arrow labelled "Authorised excerpts".

GROUP 5 heading: "LLM answer"
Body: "Use only authorised excerpts"
Small shield/check motif below: "Recheck access before delivery"
This means the backend rechecks access; do NOT imply the LLM makes permission decisions.

BOTTOM STRIP across the content width, subtle mint, exact:
"Permission change → next request uses current access"
Smaller second line:
"Dataset remains selectable · No authorised evidence → safe response, no answer-model call"
Small, unobtrusive provenance line at the very bottom:
"Recorded source ACLs + current local permissions"

Make the project, Slack conversation access and clearance rules prominent enough to understand at presentation scale. Keep the original elegant style, English only, all text accurate, no extra features or claims, no POSIX, no external PDP, no real-time source-sync claim, no decorative giant padlocks, no tiny dense footnotes. Preserve the complete database/search/answer pipeline.
